label: B-skills-on

review.summary: The tests for the new skill budget helpers cover only the happy path and miss several important cases: input validation for fitSkillsToBudget, the missing-skill error path in loadSkillBodies, and the skip-and-fit algorithm logic. Additionally, the loadSkillBodies test makes a weak assertion. These gaps mean that realistic bugs (invalid budget, missing skills, broken algorithm) would not be caught.

findings.title: Missing test for skip-and-fit logic in fitSkillsToBudget
findings.rationale: The algorithm skips an enabled skill that exceeds remaining budget but may include a smaller one later. The test only has one enabled skill that fits; it does not verify this behavior.
findings.suggestion: Add a test with a large skill that does not fit and a smaller one that does, e.g. [{id:'big', tokens:200, enabled:true},{id:'small', tokens:50, enabled:true}] with budget 100 -> expected ['small'].

findings.title: Untested input validation in fitSkillsToBudget
findings.rationale: The guard at line 14 throws RangeError for non-positive or non-integer budget. No test exercises this path. A regression that removes or inverts the guard would go unnoticed.
findings.suggestion: Add tests with budget = 0, -1, 1.5 expecting RangeError.

findings.title: Untested error path in loadSkillBodies
findings.rationale: At line 35, if repo.getBody returns undefined, a NotFoundError is thrown. The test only supplies a mock that always returns '# x', so the error path is never exercised.
findings.suggestion: Add a test where repo.getBody returns undefined for one id, then await expect(loadSkillBodies(...)).rejects.toThrow(NotFoundError).

findings.title: Weak assertion in loadSkillBodies test
findings.rationale: The test only checks that `bodies` is defined. A wrong implementation (e.g., returning a map with a different key or no value) would still pass.
findings.suggestion: Assert the actual content: `expect(bodies.get('a')).toBe('# x')` and verify map size.
